To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
self regulated learning in tertiary mathematics education, and particularly that of engineering students, is a complex and multi faceted phenomenon.
(meta )cognition, motivation and behavior play an important role in self regulated learning in higher education in general as well as mathematics tertiary education in particular.
self regulated learning in tertiary mathematics education, as well as the support for it, is a multi layered and multi dimensional construct.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether and how the use of self regulated learning strategies can be supported.
the question of how students learn in mathematics tertiary education, especially engineering students.
the question how engineering students can be supported to successfully study mathematics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

students' self regulated learning in engineering tertiary education should be supported by offering them a variety of learning offers and learning opportunities which are well aligned with their goals and needs, as perceived by the students.
self regulated learning in tertiary mathematics education is an important and promising field for research.
students' self regulated learning can be supported by a combination of various learning offers, which can be implemented in different ways and at different points in time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students in mathematics tertiary courses are highly motivated, but they are also highly stressed and thus need support in their learning process.
students in higher education are able to regulate their learning to a certain extent.
students' self regulated learning is not a fixed entity, but rather a dynamic and changeable process which is influenced by a variety of factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
self regulated learning in tertiary education is not just a matter of individual students' abilities and skills.
self regulated learning is a complex phenomenon, which cannot be reduced to a single factor.
students are able to regulate their learning in mathematics tertiary courses, even though they often have to overcome various difficulties.
